futureDescription: We are confident that one day in the near future, Urhobo will become the official language of the Urhobo Nation, taught in schools and spoken in Urhobo communities with pride and love. Together, we can create the Urhobo world.

languageDescription: The Urhobo language is a beautiful, expressive, tonal language that, unfortunately, has not been spoken officially in the Urhobo Nation for many years. Consequently, over time, parts of the language have been forgotten, and sadly lost.
missionDescription: Guọnọ is a tech startup dedicated to providing services in the Urhobo language. Our goal is to help revive, promote, and document the Urhobo language.

classesCardTitle: Urhobo classes, one learner at a time
classesCardDescription: Learn Urhobo with a personal coach. Start with Migwo and grow at your own pace.
dashboardClassesDescription: Apply for personal Urhobo classes and build your language skills with a coach.
classesSubtitle: Personal Urhobo classes built around you — your level, your goals and your schedule. Start with Migwo and grow into confident conversation.
classesProofDiaspora: For learners at home and abroad
whyUrhoboTitle: Why Urhobo? Why learn with a person?
reconnectRootsDescription: You are Urhobo by birth or by family. Learn the language your parents and grandparents spoke — not just from a textbook, but from a real person who lives the culture.
speakWithFamilyDescription: Talk with your parents, grandparents and relatives across Delta State — Ughelli, Warri, Sapele, Udu, Okpe, Uvwie, Agbarho, Abraka and beyond — without needing someone to translate for you.
keepLanguageAliveDescription: Millions of people speak Urhobo in Delta State, Nigeria. Every new learner helps carry the language, stories and traditions to the next generation.
learningPathTitle: Your learning path — the Urhobo way
learningPathDescription: From Migwo to confident conversation. Each level builds on the last with app practice between classes.
level1Description: Migwo, Vren, Udi, yes and no, and introducing yourself
level2Description: Parents, siblings, family words and everyday home life
level3Description: Food, cooking, buying and selling, and market numbers
level4Description: Counting, time, days of the week and celebrations
level5Description: Proverbs, folktales and the art of storytelling
level6Description: Traditions, respect language, naming ceremonies and festivals
level7Title: Level 7 — Fluent Urhobo: Speak with confidence
level7Description: Hold real conversations, tell stories and speak with family
classStep1Description: Fill in the short form. Tell us your level, goals, dialect and where you are based.
classStep2Description: A 15-minute call to find your level: complete beginner, understand but don't speak, a little, conversational or fluent.
classStep3Description: We match you with a coach based on your dialect (Ughelli, Okpe, Uvwie and more), goals and availability.
classStep4Title: 4. Weekly live class + daily app practice
classStep4Description: One-to-one classes on Zoom / Google Meet / WhatsApp, plus 15–30 minutes of practice in the Guọnọ app.
includedDescription: Live classes, a personal learning plan, pronunciation coaching, cultural context, recorded lessons and WhatsApp support.
diasporaFriendlyDescription: Times for Lagos / WAT, London / GMT, US Eastern and Canada. Pay in Naira or USD.
coach1Description: Calm, encouraging and great with complete beginners and children. Teaches everyday spoken Urhobo.
coach2Description: Helps diaspora learners speak confidently with family. Focuses on natural, everyday conversation.
coach3Description: Specialises in Ita (proverbs), storytelling, tradition, weddings and formal occasions.
pricingDescription: Free application • Free first placement call • Cancel anytime • Pay in Naira or USD
intensiveSessions: 12 classes per month or family classes
faqWhoAnswer: Anyone aged 5 and up — children, adults, diaspora learners and complete beginners. No prior Urhobo is needed.
faqDialectAnswer: You will learn standard spoken Urhobo. Your coach adapts lessons to your family dialect — Ughelli, Warri, Uvwie, Okpe, Udu, Agbarho, Sapele, Abraka and others.
faqNeedAnswer: A phone or computer, 15–30 minutes a day, and a willingness to speak. Live classes run on Zoom / Google Meet / WhatsApp.
faqMissQuestion: What happens if I miss a class?
faqMissAnswer: Reschedule at least 12 hours before the class at no extra cost. You can also catch up with the recording.
faqKidsAnswer: Yes. Coaches are vetted, parents get a short update after each class, and lessons can be recorded.
faqGuaranteeQuestion: What if it is not for me?
faqGuaranteeAnswer: If the first live class is not right for you, you pay nothing. There is no long-term contract.
story1Quote: I started without a word of Urhobo. Three months later I surprised my grandmother in Ughelli on the phone. She cried.
story2Quote: My son now greets his grandmother in Urhobo on video calls without me prompting him.
story3Quote: I learned Urhobo for my traditional wedding. My in-laws were amazed — it made the day.
